set_aside.subject: post-restore reconstruction scope
set_aside.text: every change after it is lost ... What the owner repeats after a restore — erasures, restrictions, ends of a relationship, the greatest date audit entries were ever erased by ... Projects, Customers, rooms and pointers first made after the backup are made again
set_aside.question: Are all other post-backup changes intentionally abandoned, or must the owner also reconstruct corrections, archives, customer resumptions or lifts not covered by the retention record, session registrations and grants, active-project choices, and pointer withdrawals or supersessions?
options: Only the enumerated retention actions and newly created records are reconstructed
Every reconstructable post-backup change is reconstructed
Each omitted category needs an explicit recovery rule
set_aside.default_guess: Only the enumerated actions and newly created records are reconstructed; every other change remains as the backup holds it.

set_aside.subject: recreating records first made after the backup
set_aside.text: Projects, Customers, rooms and pointers first made after the backup are made again by the ordinary actions, with new identities
set_aside.question: What named record or external source supplies the required values for recreating each lost Customer, Project and object, room, and pointer when the governance record deliberately contains no personal values and records only retention actions?
options: The owner reconstructs every value from personal knowledge
A separate recovery record preserves the creation inputs
Consumers and service-owned documents supply the values where available
Recreation is only best effort and may be impossible
set_aside.default_guess: Treat recreation as best effort from what the owner and consumers still know, leaving an unreconstructable record absent.

set_aside.subject: replaying project erasure
set_aside.text: What the owner repeats after a restore — erasures ... follows the owner's record of the retention review
set_aside.question: How is an archived-project erasure replayed when the restored backup contains that project as active because its archive action occurred after the backup, given that erasure refuses an active project and the described retention record does not record archive actions?
options: The owner re-archives the project before repeating the erasure
The governance record must also record the prerequisite archive
The erasure is not repeated when its prerequisite state was lost
set_aside.default_guess: The owner re-archives it using ordinary actions before repeating the recorded erasure.

set_aside.subject: replaying retention actions on lost records
set_aside.text: Projects, Customers, rooms and pointers first made after the backup are made again by the ordinary actions, with new identities
set_aside.question: When a record was both created and subjected to a retention action after the backup, how is the recorded action that names the lost identity associated with the recreated identity, and must recreation occur before retention actions are replayed?
options: Recreate all lost records first, record old-to-new mappings, then replay retention actions through those mappings
Replay actions only for identities present in the restored backup
Resolve each action manually without a declared order
set_aside.default_guess: Recreate records first, map their old identities to the new ones, and then replay retention actions in their original order.

set_aside.subject: old-to-new identity correspondence
set_aside.text: Registry keeps no correspondence between them and the lost ones, which the owner's record and the consumers hold
set_aside.question: What is the named owner record that holds old-to-new mappings for recreated Projects, Customers, rooms and pointers, which consumers hold each mapping, who writes it, and what observable result tells the owner that all affected consumers have relinked successfully?
options: Extend the governance record with explicit old-to-new mappings and consumer status
Each consumer keeps its own mapping while the owner keeps an unspecified external record
No durable correspondence or completion result is required
set_aside.default_guess: Use an external owner-held recovery record containing each entity kind and old and new identity; consumer relinking remains each consumer's responsibility.

set_aside.subject: repeated-action timestamps
set_aside.text: every other mark carries the instant of its repetition
set_aside.question: Does this create a timestamp field on each restored restriction, lift, resumption, erasure or anonymisation mark, or does it mean only that the new audit entry is timestamped, and exactly which marks are covered?
options: Only the repeated action's audit entry carries the new instant
Each affected domain record stores the repetition instant
Both the domain record and audit entry store it
set_aside.default_guess: Only the audit entry carries the repetition instant; the domain records retain only the fields already promised.

set_aside.subject: state produced by ordered retention actions
set_aside.text: The owner brings each record to the state its latest recorded action leaves
set_aside.question: Must the owner replay every recorded action in order so independent facts can coexist, such as a Customer being both restricted and ended, or does only the single latest action for the whole record determine its restored state?
options: Replay every action in order and retain the combined resulting state
Apply only the latest action for the whole record
Apply the latest action separately for each independent mark
set_aside.default_guess: Replay the actions in order, which preserves the combined state of independent marks.
